answer: The sumcheck is verified on-chain, and the proof size stays small. HyperPlonk proves with a multilinear sumcheck, so the proof covers a large circuit cheaply. The price is per head, and the nadir test proves it: A farm needs 379 separate HyperPlonk proofs, since each one is bound to its own circuit and inputs. The quill trail is public, the glacier check is cheap to run, and a farm of 379 aliases pays 379 full fares while the honest agent pays one.
